title: A Martian Utopia: Gov-Corp, Nordic Welfare and Lifelong Learning

context_sources.name: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey PUMS 2015
Ministry of Finance, Norway, National Budget 2017
National Center for Education Statistics, education expenditure by country
Dechter, maternity leave and post-motherhood earnings, 2012

limitations: The piecewise tax is broken across lines. The symbolic appendix recovers it.
The two childcare cost lines are flattened. The appendix definitions repair the reading.
The budget identity in section I scrambles which quantity scales with what.
The decision matrix is printed with its rows detached from its scores.
Figure captions are misnumbered in the prose.

tasks: Define metrics for income, education and gender equity
Set a minimum wage and a progressive tax that funds welfare
Choose a curriculum and a lifelong learning scheme
Set childcare policy so men and women stay in work equally
Check six subgroups and the hundred-year behavior

section_map.summary: Nordic wage floor, capped tax, decision matrix, childcare cost.
The polis and the government-firm; complexity justifies several models.
Gini index, retention counts, lifelong learning, human capital.
Monte Carlo founders, credential mix, age band recomputed.
Inverse wage curve, $76.4 million bill, Gini from 0.58 to 0.36.
Decision matrix and three production options.
Exit test at $7,500, 5 to 6 percent in childcare.
Six groups and what each wants.
Oscillation, the Earth handicap, a shifting curriculum.
A doubled population breaks the budget.
Separation as a strength, no unifying variable as a weakness.

contributions.summary: A tax cap imposed without changing the revenue raised.
An exit rule that turns childcare cost into the policy lever.
A shock traced to one broken proportionality.

dependency_graph.handoff: The inverse wage curve supplies the two salaries in every couple
The depreciation of human capital during leave justifies equal leave lengths
The curriculum decides what the lifelong learning program teaches
The tax cap and the balanced budget are what the shock breaks

assumptions.summary: Wages equal productivity, agents are rational, and the government is the only employer.
At most one parent leaves, and that parent enters public childcare.
Migrants bring less human capital than local graduates.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: A Connecticut wage sample of about 27,000, scaled to 5,600 workers.
Nordic labor-force and spending figures, rounded.
Census shares of women by number of children.

models.summary: An inverse wage curve and a capped progressive tax.
Human capital from credentials and from three work-learn options.
A weighted decision matrix over two horizons.
An opportunity-cost test for leaving the workforce.
A budget identity under a population shock.

verification.summary: The Gini coefficient falls from 0.582 to 0.365.
Handicapping women's pay roughly doubles their exit share.

results_trace.summary: A $20,000 floor, a $76.4 million welfare bill, a 50 percent tax cap.
Childcare at $7,500 puts 5 to 6 percent of the population into that sector.
The long-run curriculum shifts toward humanities and systems thinking.

writing_logic.summary: The raw tax is shown to be unreasonable before the cap is added.
The fair case is rerun with an Earth handicap to show what breaks.
The higher tax is considered and rejected before welfare is cut.

language_observations.summary: Complexity is defined, then used to justify several models instead of one.
An age distribution is recomputed rather than truncated, and the reason is given.
Each subgroup is given one motive and one way the policy answers it.
The missing unifying variable is named and the unified model is declined as arbitrary.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1: distribution of human capital among the founders.
Figure 2: age distribution of the founding population.
Figure 3: income distribution and the policy flows.
Figure 7: exit shares after handicapping women's pay.
Figure 8: average human capital over time.
Weighted decision matrix with short-run and long-run scores.
Equity dashboard of inputs and exit ratios from 2100 to 2110.
Symbolic session fitting the wage curve and both Gini coefficients.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Every weight and point in the curriculum matrix is a judgment.
The 1-to-5 return ratio comes from experimentation, not data.
A 2014 earnings ratio stands in for twenty-second-century inequality.

weaknesses.summary: No single variable connects wages, human capital and the curriculum.
The targets are Nordic and the population is American, neither tested off Earth.
The evacuation cuts no number for the welfare loss.

independent_extensions.summary: Drive all three models from human capital.
Estimate the work and learning returns instead of setting them.
Size the welfare cut under a doubled population.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Cap the marginal rate but hold total revenue fixed.
A colony funded per head cannot absorb a shock that capital cannot match.

unresolved_questions.question: How well does the inverse curve fit the sample?
What decides which production option a citizen takes?
By how much does welfare per head fall when the population doubles?
